title: HTTP/3 WebSocket TCP Forwarder Verification
verification_method: Focused HTTP/3 WebSocket loopback test with a local TCP echo server, adjacent RFC 9220 regression tests, SpecTrace JSON validation, generated coverage triage, and diff hygiene.
scope: This verification covers an accepted RFC 9220 WebSocket Extended CONNECT tunnel whose application handler connects to a local TCP echo server, forwards a masked client binary WebSocket payload into TCP, returns the TCP response as an unmasked binary WebSocket message, and echoes a WebSocket close frame before FIN.
preconditions: The WebSocket frame parser remains trace-owned by `VER-QUIC-RFC9220-0002`.
The WebSocket handler dispatch boundary remains trace-owned by `VER-QUIC-RFC9220-0003`.
Accepted tunnel message helpers remain trace-owned by `VER-QUIC-RFC9220-0004`.
Received ping/pong control handling remains trace-owned by `VER-QUIC-RFC9220-0005`.
Bounded TCP response chunking remains trace-owned by `VER-QUIC-RFC9220-0015`.
expected_result: The focused TCP forwarder and adjacent WebSocket regression tests pass, the new RFC 9220 TCP forwarder requirement is trace-clean, SpecTrace validation accepts the artifacts, and diff hygiene is clean.
status_summary: The HTTP/3 WebSocket handler surface now has locally verified binary tunnel forwarding through a caller-supplied TCP stream. Evidence class is local same-process HTTP/3 QUIC loopback plus local loopback TCP; it is not external peer interoperability, published ProtocolLab evidence, or isolated-host proof.
